s1.syndrome_frame: Acute collapse with recurrent ventricular arrhythmias
key_facts: Patient is a woman in her 50s
Collapsed at home
Received chest compressions from her husband
Recovered consciousness at home
Vital signs were normal on admission
Physical examination was unremarkable
ECG showed sinus rhythm with normal QRS and QT intervals
ECG showed repetitive monomorphic premature ventricular complexes
Short-coupling interval of 240 milliseconds
Serum electrolyte levels were normal
Transthoracic echocardiography showed normal cardiac function and structure
Emergency coronary angiography showed no evidence of obstructive coronary artery disease
Genetic testing revealed a variant of unknown significance in the RyR2 gene

shortlist.label: Catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia
shortlist.why_kept: Repetitive monomorphic premature ventricular complexes and polymorphic ventricular tachycardia are characteristic of this condition

shortlist.label: Ryanodine receptor type 2 mutation-related arrhythmias
shortlist.why_kept: Genetic testing revealed a variant of unknown significance in the RyR2 gene, which is associated with this condition

shortlist.label: Familial polymorphic ventricular tachycardia
shortlist.why_kept: Similar to CPVT, this condition is characterized by recurrent ventricular arrhythmias and may be related to the RyR2 gene variant

shortlist.label: Idiopathic ventricular fibrillation
shortlist.why_kept: Normal cardiac structure and function, absence of obstructive coronary artery disease, and presence of ventricular fibrillation episodes

shortlist.label: Arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy
shortlist.why_kept: Although less likely given normal echocardiography, this condition can present with ventricular arrhythmias and may not always have overt structural abnormalities

raw.rationale: The patient's ECG showed repetitive monomorphic premature ventricular complexes with a short-coupling interval, and episodes of polymorphic ventricular tachycardia, which are characteristic of catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia (CPVT). The normal cardiac structure and function, as well as the absence of obstructive coronary artery disease, also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Ryanodine receptor type 2 mutation-related arrhythmias
rejected.why: Although the patient has a variant of unknown significance in the RyR2 gene, the clinical presentation and ECG findings are more consistent with CPVT.

rejected.label: Familial polymorphic ventricular tachycardia
rejected.why: There is no mention of a family history of similar arrhythmias or sudden cardiac death, which is often a feature of familial polymorphic ventricular tachycardia.

rejected.label: Idiopathic ventricular fibrillation
rejected.why: The patient's ECG shows a clear pattern of premature ventricular complexes and polymorphic ventricular tachycardia, which suggests a specific underlying mechanism rather than an idiopathic cause.

rejected.label: Arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: The patient's echocardiography and coronary angiography results show normal cardiac structure and function, which is not consistent with arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy.
